clue.text: French film actor opens his own sound stage

indicators.note: the actor opens the other piece by going into it, splitting it apart

parts.note: in French, son means both 'his' and 'sound', so the phrase points to the French word
Jacques Tati, French comic actor and director of Monsieur Hulot's Holiday

explanation.surface: A French comedian launches a new film studio of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound stage' looks like one film-studio term, but 'sound' belongs to the wordplay and 'stage' alone is the definition; 'opens' means the actor goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage on a journey is a stopping place, as a railway or coaching stop is.

clue.text: Firm supports explorer sailing north for Virginia, say

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it
in a down clue, travelling north means the explorer's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: John Cabot, the Venetian navigator who sailed to North America for England
CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company backs a navigator heading north towards the colony of Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virginia' sounds like the American state the explorer might sail for; it is a variety of leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia is a well-known type of cured leaf grown for smoking, named after the American state.

clue.text: Iberian writers use this until designers restrict it

indicators.note: the two words enclose the sought letters, keeping them confined within

explanation.surface: Spanish and Portuguese authors may use something until the design people forbid it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish writes a wavy mark over n, and Portuguese over a and o, so writers of Iberia need it.

clue.text: Language of old volume, one with strap

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetres, is a unit of volume
I is the Roman numeral for one
to tan someone is to beat them, as with a strap

explanation.surface: An old book of some language, held together with a strap.
explanation.definitionFit: Occitan is the Romance tongue of southern France, the langue d'oc of the troubadours.

clue.text: Call this writer for part of speech?

parts.note: to call someone is to ring or telephone them
the setter referring to himself, giving the pronoun me

explanation.surface: Ring me to learn which grammatical category a word belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of speech' suggests noun or verb; here it means a unit of spoken sound, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A phoneme is a smallest distinct unit of sound in a language, literally one part of spoken speech.

clue.text: Unionist visiting Hampshire's favourite spots

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so the one letter enters the county abbreviation

parts.note: Hants is the standard abbreviation of Hampshire, an English county on the south coast
U is the abbreviation for Unionist, as in Northern Ireland politics

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish politician tours the best-loved places in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: HANTS is the usual abbreviation for Hampshire, a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: One's haunts are places frequented often, the familiar spots a person keeps returning to.

clue.text: Queen's hat back to front in northeast India

definitions.note: read as 'Queen is', the 's joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: the turned headgear sits between the other two pieces

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for northeast
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the front half of the word is moved round to the back

parts.note: titfer is Cockney rhyming slang for hat, from tit-for-tat

explanation.surface: A queen's headgear is worn the wrong way round in north-east India.
explanation.walkthrough: Titfer is Cockney rhyming slang (tit-for-tat, hat); 'back to front' swaps its halves before it goes 'in' the compass point and the phonetic letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was the Egyptian queen, wife of Akhenaten, famed for her painted bust.

clue.text: Sheep tucked into natural food, a lifesaver

indicators.note: the animal is placed within the other word, as if eating into it

parts.note: mast is the fallen nuts of beech and oak, a natural food for pigs
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A sheep that gorges on natural forage turns out to be someone's salvation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked into' suggests the sheep eating its fodder; it means the animal sits inside the word for beech-nut forage.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen in the Second World War nicknamed their inflatable life jacket after the buxom film star.

clue.text: Count on pair in complex, so to speak?

indicators.note: something complex is intricate and tangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman relies on a couple living in a housing complex, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is taken literally: the way one speaks, the manner of saying words aloud.

clue.text: Top brand, The Third Man

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a label is a brand, a trade name

explanation.surface: A leading make is advertised with the title of the Orson Welles film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Third Man' looks like the film; it means the third male in Genesis, after Adam and Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man is Adam, then his sons Cain and this brother, the third man.

clue.text: Posh male and female interrupt round 10 and 12, for example

indicators.note: the three letters break into the shape word, splitting it

parts.note: a round is a circle
U means upper-class, as in Nancy Mitford's U and non-U
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Upper-class men and women break into a round of light entries and stresses.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to another light but is just ten, the Roman X; '12' does refer to light 12.
explanation.definitionFit: This hat-shaped mark over a vowel is one kind of stress or pronunciation sign, as light 12 names.

clue.text: Stress papers should be removed from crash

indicators.note: this tells us one piece is taken out of the other

parts.note: a crash is an accident
ID, identity documents, are one's papers

explanation.surface: Pressure to produce identity documents should be taken away from a car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress on a syllable is the emphasis given to it in speech.

clue.text: Public officials sign new books at the front

indicators.note: the two short pieces are placed before the zodiac sign

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Officials sign fresh books placed at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Notaries are officials authorised to witness and certify documents for the public.

clue.text: Film barbarian, tense, seizing child's letter

indicators.note: one piece grabs and holds the other within it

parts.note: Conan the Barbarian, the film role played by Arnold Schwarzenegger
a son is a child; the 's is read as 'has'
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A movie barbarian, nervous, grabs a child's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters divide into vowels and the others, any of which counts as one.

clue.text: Brief stop in house on section of canal

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
the colon is a section of the alimentary canal, the gut

explanation.surface: A short halt at a house beside a stretch of canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canal' suggests a waterway; it is the alimentary canal. A SEMI is a British semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark makes a pause shorter than a full stop, so a brief halt.

clue.text: Measure diameter with circles

indicators.note: one word goes round the other, surrounding it

explanation.surface: Instructions to measure the diameter of some circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth from side to side is a dimension one measures.

clue.text: Stripped hammock back, revealing insect

indicators.note: the remaining letters are read backwards
stripping takes off the outer layer, so the first and last letters go

explanation.surface: A stripped-down hammock at the back reveals a creepy-crawly.
explanation.definitionFit: The comma is a butterfly named for the white comma-shaped mark beneath its wing.

clue.text: Swapping parts, extract unused frames

indicators.note: the two halves of the phrase change places

parts.note: to extract is to take out

explanation.surface: Exchanging components, removing frames nobody used.
explanation.definitionFit: Film footage cut and left out of the final edit is called this.

clue.text: Briefly ring reviewer Mark

indicators.note: a brief word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to ring someone is to dial them
a critic reviews books, films and plays

explanation.surface: Give a critic a quick call, Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name being addressed; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A diacritic is any mark added to a letter to show its sound, such as a cedilla.

clue.text: Mark at bottom of letter: "Edward has to wear black"

indicators.note: the wearer goes inside what is worn, so one name is placed within the other

parts.note: Cilla Black, the Liverpool singer and TV presenter
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Footnote to a letter: Edward must wear black to a funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black' suggests mourning; it is Cilla Black, a British pop singer and presenter of the TV show Blind Date.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedilla is the hook placed under c, as in the French word façade.

clue.text: They lean forward to indicate species in text

definitions.text: They lean forward to indicate species in text

parts.words: They lean forward to indicate species in text
parts.note: a sloping typeface, by convention used for Latin species names in printed writing

explanation.surface: Something that leans forward to signal a species in a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping type leans to the right and biological names like Homo sapiens are set in it.

clue.text: It was used to shoot two Brits in Victoria

indicators.note: the word is given twice over

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for a Briton, and Victoria is an Australian state

explanation.surface: A gun used to shoot two Britons in Melbourne's state.
explanation.walkthrough: POM is Australian slang for a British person; Victoria is a state of Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The pom-pom was a quick-firing gun used in the Boer War and as a naval anti-aircraft weapon.

clue.text: Last project

definitions.meaning: to last is to endure to the finish, to keep going
to project is to protrude, jut from a surface

explanation.surface: The final project.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to endure to the end and to jut out.

clue.text: Bookmark: Use Drugs

parts.note: to do drugs is to use them
gear is slang for drugs

explanation.surface: A bookmark tells readers to take drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A folded-down page corner is a makeshift way to keep one's place in a book.

clue.text: Solemn Queen presented bandages

indicators.note: a bandage wraps around something, so one word encloses the letter

parts.note: to present is to give, so presented is gave
R is Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A serious monarch handed out dressings.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave means serious and sober in manner.

clue.text: Bug leading staff on phone survey

parts.note: to bug is to annoy or gall
up means ahead or leading, as in a match

indicators.note: heard over the telephone, so the word for staff is given by its sound

parts.note: a pole is a staff

explanation.surface: A telephone survey about bugging the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: The American Gallup organisation runs well-known opinion surveys.

clue.text: A big shot at Old Trafford backed league

indicators.note: taken in reverse, read from end to start

parts.note: a six is the biggest hit in cricket, and Old Trafford in Manchester is a Test cricket ground

explanation.surface: A star player at Manchester United's ground supported the league.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Trafford suggests football, but there is also a cricket ground of that name in Manchester; a hit over the boundary scores SIX.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis was the wartime alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan, a league of nations.

clue.text: Can celebrity, Le Carré for one?

parts.note: can is slang for prison, as is pen, short for penitentiary
a big name is a celebrity

explanation.surface: Can a famous person be John le Carré?
explanation.definitionFit: John le Carré was the assumed writing name of David Cornwell, a famous example of an author's alias.

clue.text: Orient sections to fill newspaper

indicators.note: one piece fills the other, going inside it

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
areas are sections or parts

explanation.surface: Instructions to arrange sections to fill a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orient' looks like a verb meaning arrange; it is the noun, the East. The FT is the Financial Times, a London business daily.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is the East, especially the countries of eastern Asia.
